mediaWork.title: Grace and Justice on Death Row: The Race against Time and Texas to Free an Innocent Man
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Wrongful conviction, death penalty, prosecutorial misconduct, attorney-client relationship
mediaWork.summaryNotes: The book details the legal battle to free Alfred Dewayne Brown from death row, exploring the attorney-client relationship that evolved into a deep brotherhood. It provides a firsthand account of flaws in the criminal justice system, offering a story of hope and redemption.  The foreword is by Sister Helen Prejean.  The book highlights Brown's wrongful conviction for capital murder, focusing on prosecutorial misconduct, withheld evidence, and coerced witness testimony.
